issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Violated Values: I acted in ways that go against who I am
issues.explanation: For a rape trauma profile, the appraisal 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' is the only item that implies perpetration or morally troubling behaviour by the patient. Paired with memory items centered on terror and shame and trigger items tied to tiredness, driving with others, and sounds, this appraisal is hard to reconcile clinically with the rest of the profile and with the trauma type. The other negative appraisals reflect mistrust and loss of faith, which fit sexual assault trauma; this item instead points toward a different moral injury formulation and creates an internal mismatch within the Negative Appraisals node.

vignette: James, a 53-year-old bus driver from North America, has been struggling with persistent symptoms following a traumatic event. Married and deeply affected by his experience, James reports feeling extremely tired and exhausted most days. This fatigue is often exacerbated when he is driving passengers around the city, especially in environments where sounds remind him of the assault. On one particularly exhausting day, James found himself behind the wheel of his bus, the engine’s hum echoing through the empty seats. Suddenly, the sound of a car horn triggered an overwhelming flashback. As he relived the terrifying event, he felt the same sense of terror and shame that had overwhelmed him during the actual assault. The memory replayed like a film in his mind, and with each vivid detail, James was transported back to the night when everything changed. James had come to believe that people could not be trusted; after the traumatic experience, his faith in humanity was shattered. He felt intense shame about what happened to his body, and these negative appraisals only intensified every time he recalled the event. The memories became more vivid and distressing each time they surfaced, making it almost impossible for James to separate his current life from the trauma. The weight of these thoughts made daily tasks, especially driving, increasingly difficult. Every noise on the road seemed to be a potential trigger, leading him to feel exhausted and drained. He began avoiding routes that reminded him of the assault, even though this meant taking longer and more circuitous routes to reach his destinations. His wife noticed the changes in James’s behavior but struggled to understand why he was withdrawing from her and his usual activities. James felt increasingly isolated as his fear of encountering triggers grew stronger. The combination of feeling tired and being hyper-aware of every sound made it nearly impossible for him to perform his duties without constant vigilance. This cycle became self-reinforcing: the more he feared, the more exhausted he became, and each episode reinforced his mistrust and negative beliefs. One day, James had a particularly harrowing experience while driving through a crowded intersection. A loud siren caused him to freeze in terror, unable to focus on navigating safely. This incident was a turning point; he realized that his work and relationships were suffering significantly due to the intrusive memories and constant vigilance against triggers. James finally decided to seek help after recognizing that his symptoms had grown too intense for him to manage alone. He is most afraid of losing control while driving or failing to protect himself from triggering situations, but at the same time, he hopes to regain a sense of trust in others and find peace with his past experiences. Through therapy, James aims to navigate the complex web of triggers, memories, and negative beliefs that have engulfed his life since the assault.
